principle: Edges represent data dependency and propagation requirements, not only visual proximity. If an approved underlying field changes, all dependent modules must reflect the same current value.
state_propagation_posture: Propagate value plus standing: source/evidence basis, field truth state, scoped use, blocking effect, and authority requirement. Never propagate a naked value as project truth.

edges.propagation_rule: Activation reads PAC origin and validation fields; activation status must not overwrite PAC origin truth.
Scope begins from PAC origin data, then records later clarification as validation/operational truth downstream.
Consultant needs are triggered by scope/services signals and must remain visible until assigned or explicitly ruled out.
Contract view must expose mismatches between operational scope and authorized/contractual scope.
Activation is blocked or qualified by unknown, pending, or misaligned authorization/contract data.
Budget transforms approved fee/compensation facts but does not rewrite compensation origin data.
Compensation must indicate whether fee basis is proposal-origin, contract-authorized, UHG Service Order-derived, or unresolved.
Contract view must expose whether dates are contractual, illustrative, preliminary, owner-dependent, or incomplete.
Budget/cashflow views depend on schedule phase/milestone structure and must mark low-confidence schedule inputs.
UHG-specific required LCD/LCW fields may add contractual analysis requirements without redefining PAC as UHG-specific.
For UHG, contractually binding LCD/LCW workflow fields must be visible in contracts/authorization without becoming universal Grace PAC fields.
Consultant coordination depends on explicit responsibility assignment; unassigned triggers feed risk/gaps.
Any module may surface a gap, conflict, uncertainty, override, or archive/source-preservation need; risk/gaps is the visible worklist, not a hidden error state.
System setup proceeds only when activation conditions are satisfied or an explicit override records accepted coordination risk.
